title: Viewer closes pooled readers and deletes temp copies/folders on the main thread (stopWork, stale load, deinit, TemporaryCopies.release, ViewerPlugin.stop).
where: Viewer/UI/ViewerPane.swift:324; Viewer/Model/ByteSource.swift:499-502; Viewer/Model/ByteSource.swift:182-188; Viewer/Model/ByteSource.swift:315; Viewer/UI/ViewerPane.swift:289; Viewer/Model/ByteSource.swift:190; Viewer/UI/ViewerPane.swift:253; Viewer/UI/ViewerPane.swift:331; Viewer/UI/ViewerPane.swift:317; Viewer/UI/ViewerPane.swift:146; Viewer/UI/RichViews.swift:117; Viewer/ViewerPlugin.swift:112; Viewer/UI/RichViews.swift:127
detail: ViewerPane.stopWork calls loaded?.source.close() -> CachedByteSource.close -> ProviderByteSource.close, which calls FileReader.close() on up to activeProcessorCount idle readers, then spill.discard(). stopWork is main-only; callers are load (:251), clear (:329), ViewerWindowController.windowWillClose (:115) and QuickViewPanel.remove (:93). Same class: ViewerPane.swift:289 closes the source of a stale load on main; ProviderByteSource.deinit closes readers on whichever thread drops the last reference (main for loaded = nil at ViewerPane.swift:253 and :331); temporaryCopies.release (ViewerPane.swift:317, :146 in deinit) runs evict which calls FileManager.removeItem on main; ViewerPlugin.stop runs removeAll which deletes the whole root on main. Effect: every cursor move in quick view runs this; a network reader whose close() does a round trip stalls the UI.
fix: Hand the source and the doomed folders to a background queue to close and delete.

title: TextPagerView can be deallocated on an indexing thread (self? temporary strong reference in buildIndex progress callback).
detail: Medium-low. document.buildIndex(parallel:) { self?.indexProgressed() } takes a temporary strong reference on a concurrentPerform or global worker for the duration of indexProgressed. If main drops its reference (window close, quick view hidden) while the worker holds the +1, the worker's release is the last and NSView dealloc and deinit (including NSScroller subviews) run off-main.
fix: Capture a small non-view coalescer object (the lock and flag) and take the view strongly only inside the main.async.

title: Pause does not pause parallel checksum jobs: ToolRun.advance holds reportLock across a blocking monitor.report.
detail: Medium-low. ToolRun.advance holds reportLock across monitor.report, which enters PauseGate.passWhenOpen and blocks while paused. Every other hashing thread (ChecksumFiles.swift:216, Parallel pool threads) takes the non-forced path where reportLock.try() fails and it returns and keeps hashing. One thread pauses and the rest finish the job; the job thread then blocks at the forced advance (FileToolsPlugin.swift:125). ProgressMeter (SpaceCalculator.swift:46-53) holds its lock across the report so there every thread stops; the two are inconsistent.
fix: Call gate.passWhenOpen from every thread, outside reportLock.

title: CommentStore remembers a stale read after a write (load racing setComment/forget).
detail: Low-medium. T1: comments(in:) is in load (:198). T2: setComment moves the new file into place and calls forget (:265, :208-212). T1 then stores the old comments with a fresh timestamp (:199-201). save's completion reloads the panels at once, so the Comment column gets the old text and, per the ContentColumn contract, the panel keeps it.
fix: A per-key generation bumped by forget; remember only if it is unchanged.

title: TemporaryCopies owner key outlives its pane, and removeAll races an in-flight copy.

B1: realpath() on main for every watched panel folder hangs the app on a stalled mount.
detail: Path: PanelCoordinator.panelDidChangeLocation -> updateWatchers -> LocalFileSystem.watch -> DirectoryWatcher.watch -> resolve. A virtual list forwards up to 512 folders through the same route.

title: B2: OpenArchive.capabilities takes a lock that background threads hold across I/O, blocking main from the validation tick/menu.

Trigger: a panel inside a ZIP on a stalled mount (30-600 s on the next tick), or a 1M-entry ZIP being flushed or re-read (estimated 0.5 s to several seconds).

Deadlock at quit: archive flush timer holding flushLock against ArchivesPlugin.stop() on main (lock plus main.sync cycle L5 -> MAIN -> L5).
where: Archives/OpenArchive.swift:752; Archives/OpenArchive.swift:1045; Archives/OpenArchive.swift:1362; Archives/OpenArchive.swift:1373; Archives/OpenArchive.swift:1379; Network/FTPSession.swift:133; Network/FTPSession.swift:163; Network/FTPSession.swift:169; Network/SFTPSession.swift:119; AFMKernel/PluginAPI/Kernel.swift:102; AFMShell/App/Shell.swift:109; Archives/ArchivesPlugin.swift:96
detail: Timer path (reviewer): OpenArchive.timerFired -> flush takes flushLock -> upload -> outer provider write/move/item. If the outer provider is FTP or SFTP and needs a new connection, it reaches askCredentials/askToTrust/askSecret -> Kernel.askUser -> DispatchQueue.main.sync. Main path: applicationWillTerminate -> Kernel.shutdown -> ArchivesPlugin.stop -> flushAll -> flush -> flushLock.lock(). The timer holds flushLock, main blocks on it, then the connection asks. applicationShouldTerminate drains only the job queue; the timer is not a job. Both halves read; the write path into the ask sites was not traced line by line.
fix: Never take flushLock on main. Flush in applicationShouldTerminate (.terminateLater) on a background thread with a cancellable flag and a 'Saving archives...' sheet, and add a shutdown flag that timer flushes honour.

title: VirtualFileSystem.Coalescer calls onChange on a global queue, violating the main-thread contract (panel reload off main).
detail: Coalescer.signal fires the first report on the caller (main), then schedules settle() on DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated); settle calls fire() = onChange([virtual]) = PanelCoordinator.reloadChangedPanels -> PanelViewController.reload (MainThread.assert). Trigger: two changes within 0.5 s in any watched branch view or file list. Debug builds assert; release builds race on panel and AppKit state. The provider contract says onChange is called on main. A pending settle also fires after the watcher was released.
fix: Schedule settle on DispatchQueue.main, and give Coalescer a cancelled flag set from Watchers.deinit.

title: Race, possible data loss on Move into an archive: evict can detach archive X between ArchiveFileSystem.write resolving it and openWriters += 1.
detail: Medium-high. Path A: ArchiveFileSystem.write resolves X with Slot.lock released, then calls X.write. Path B: evict sees X.isBusy == false and removes X from the store. If B runs between A's resolve and A's openWriters += 1, X is detached holding pending changes. store.commit(url) finds nothing pending and returns success, and FileJob.flushDeferred then deletes the sources. At quit flushAll misses X and the scratch folder is deleted. Narrow window.
fix: Retire an archive atomically under its own lock and have mutators re-resolve on a 'retired' error, or track busy archives in the store.

title: FTPReader.close() can interrupt a recycled connection: connection captured under stateLock, unlocked, then interrupt() called.
detail: Meanwhile the reading thread reaches EOF and releases the connection to the idle pool and a third thread acquires it, getting a spurious connectionLost, which is not retried for mkdir, delete, rename or uploads.
fix: Interrupt while holding stateLock after re-reading active, as interrupt() does at :696-698.

title: Data race on cancel in FileSearch.Walk: deliver writes node.candidates = [] under the lock while checks(for:) reads it without the lock.
detail: deliver sets node.candidates = [] under condition as soon as the search is cancelled, even while pending > 0. A worker in checks(for:) reads node.candidates.count (:433) and captures node.candidates (:440) without the lock, called from list at :425 after the unlock at :423. An unsynchronised array read against a write can crash.

H1: user regexes run with no time limit and no cancellation inside a match (catastrophic backtracking hangs Selection on main, MultiRename preview/Start, FindFiles workers).
where: Selection/SelectionMask.swift:103; Selection/SelectionPlugin.swift:258; MultiRename/RenameRules.swift:163; MultiRename/RenameRules.swift:166; MultiRename/RenameRun.swift:147; MultiRename/MultiRenameSession.swift:100; MultiRename/MultiRenameSession.swift:357; FindFiles/SearchCriteria.swift:71; FindFiles/TextPattern.swift:344; FindFiles/SearchCriteria.swift:231; MultiRename/RenameRules.swift:195-204
detail: Measured: ^(\w+[ _-]?)+\.jpg$ against aaaa....png takes 0.18 s at 22 chars, 0.73 s at 24, 2.8 s at 26 (x4 per 2 chars; a 40-char name is hours). Selection: a <regex mask of that shape on the main thread hangs the whole app for good. MultiRename preview: cancellation only checked between items so shared ParallelPool threads spin and the serial preview queue never runs another preview or sort. MultiRename Start computes the same preview inside the job; the job cannot be cancelled and jobs run one after another, so every later copy/move/delete in the app is blocked until restart. FindFiles: name regex, content regex on chunks of up to about 5 MB, field-rule regex; after Cancel or closing the window the worker threads keep spinning, each such search leaves up to max(4, cores) threads burning CPU. The plain-wildcard Search & Replace has the same shape: *a*b*c*d*e* becomes chained .*? (polynomial per name).
fix: Run every user regex through enumerateMatches(options: .reportProgress) and set stop when the cancellation flag is set or a per-item deadline passes. Move Selection matching off the main thread.

title: H2: Spotlight results are collected on the main thread, one attribute fetch per result.
detail: With no criteria the query is kMDItemFSName == "*" which returns every indexed file in scope. At a million results the per-item value(forAttribute:) loop is likely several seconds of main-thread stall, plus all paths held in memory. Cost not measured.
fix: Give the NSMetadataQuery a background operationQueue, read the paths there, and cap the count.

title: M1: everything in the Selection plugin runs on the main thread, O(n) or worse (mask select, same folder, Compare Directories, foldsCase resourceValues).
where: Selection/SelectionPlugin.swift:258; Selection/SelectionPlugin.swift:342-348; Selection/SelectionPlugin.swift:354; Selection/SelectionPlugin.swift:365-373; Selection/SelectionPlugin.swift:477; Selection/SelectionPlugin.swift:486; Selection/SelectionType.swift:132; Selection/SelectionPlugin.swift:370; Selection/SelectionFile.swift:98-164; Selection/SelectionPlugin.swift:493-496
detail: Measured core cost at 1M names: Array(name.lowercased()) 0.12 s, regex firstMatch 0.36 s; add filter, MaskEntry building, name.contains('/') and setSelected on top. A path-limited or A>B mask adds pathComponents per item, about 1.1 us each, so over 1 s at 1M. 'Same folder' and Compare Directories (several normalise+lowercase passes per name) are similar. foldsCase calls resourceValues on main; blocks on a stalled network mount.
fix: Compute name lists on a background queue (with Parallel.map), then apply with a listVersion guard.

title: M2: data race on Node.candidates when a search is cancelled (unlocked read in checks(for:) vs write in deliver).
detail: Normally deliver only touches a node once pending == 0; on cancel it skips the wait and clears every remaining sibling along the current path while workers finish in-flight list()/checks(for:). A read racing a release of the array buffer can crash on Cancel.
fix: Take the candidates snapshot inside the lock in checks(for:), or pass wanted in from list.

title: M3: each cancelled search can leak its whole walk via JobStack.push after close() (Walk -> JobStack -> closures -> Walk cycle).
detail: JobStack.push does not check isClosed. A worker finishing list() after close() pushes closures that capture the Walk, pinning the FileSearch, its query (including onlyItems, possibly millions of URLs) and the nodes.
fix: guard !isClosed in push.

title: M4: no bound on memory anywhere in the search (workers never wait for delivery; results uncapped; runForDuplicates collects every file).
detail: One slow front job (a huge file, a stalled mount) lets the other threads list the rest of the tree and buffer every candidate; with an empty mask and a text search that is every file's FileItem. A 5M-hit search likely holds a few GB (estimate, not measured).
fix: A budget of undelivered candidates that pauses list jobs, and a result cap with a 'more than N' notice.

title: M5: 'Search in found files' is quadratic and ignores Cancel (reached tests every item against every folder with isInside).
detail: Runs before the cheap name check and with no cancellation check. 200k results including 20k folders is about 4x10^9 string comparisons, likely tens of minutes. The window stays on '[Searching...]', Start stays disabled, Cancel has no effect until it finishes.
fix: Put folder keys in a set and walk each item's ancestors; test the name first; poll the flag.

title: M6: duplicate finder can list one remote file twice (no identity check for non-file URLs), so deleting 'the duplicate' deletes the only copy.
detail: Non-file URLs are kept without any identity check; FileSearch de-duplicates them by absoluteString only. Trigger: two start directories that are the same remote place by another spelling or route (sftp://host/a;sftp://HOST/a, or a server-side folder symlink given as a root). Every file appears in a group with itself. Same for one share mounted twice locally (different st_dev).
fix: Refuse or mark groups on file systems that offer no file identity; at least normalise host and path, and never put two entries with an equal locationKey/provider identity in one group.

title: M7: content search and duplicate hashing read iCloud 'dataless' files (download everything, can fill the disk).
detail: Via FileHandle(forReadingFrom:). A text search over a home folder with optimised iCloud storage downloads everything.
fix: Skip SF_DATALESS (from st_flags) unless the user asks.

title: M8: Multi-Rename moves non-local items of branch views and search results into new nested folders (name taken from URL last component only for file URLs).
detail: An FTP/SFTP/archive item named by path (sub/file.txt, or the full display path) keeps that as its name. Any change then yields a name with /, and target(of:named:) resolves it below the item's own folder: .../sub/sub/file_x.txt; folder created and file moved there. Full display paths such as ftp://... mostly become 'A folder name is empty', so the tool is unusable on those lists.
fix: Take the name from the URL for all schemes.

title: M9: Undo can be pressed again while the first Undo job is queued or running (isRunning only set for Start).
detail: Both jobs capture the same last run. The second finds nothing to restore and calls replaceLastUndo(with: []), which deletes an older run that was never undone. For a swap (1<->2) the second job finds both names present and swaps again.
fix: Disable Undo and Start while any of the session's jobs is pending; check that the history's last entry is still the captured one.

title: M10: undo history of a big run is too large for the settings store (500k-file run about 100 MB of JSON in UserDefaults, decoded on main at tool open).
detail: The latest run is kept whatever its size; loaded with the defaults domain at every launch; decoded on the main thread on first access via update() -> canUndo. 100 MB is the auditor's estimate.
fix: Keep undo runs in a file of their own, read and written off the main thread, with a hard cap.

title: M11: [T4] opens every listed file with ImageIO on the preview threads (no isSpecial/non-regular/dataless check); FIFO blocks the serial preview queue; untrusted files parsed in-process.
detail: A FIFO in the list blocks that thread for good, and with it the serial preview queue. Arbitrary untrusted files are parsed in-process by ImageIO decoders. The date cache is thrown away on every list change, so one Shift+Down re-reads all files.
fix: Regular, non-dataless files only; keep content dates across reorders; consider an image-extension allow-list.

title: M12: a regex-stuck or FIFO-stuck preview also blocks sorts (sorts and previews share one serial queue).
detail: Consequence of H1 and M11.

title: L1: stack overflow on a very long 'Find text' (recursion once per character on 512 KB threads).
detail: A 20,000-character text that occurs in a file crashed with a bus error in tp/; 12,000 passed.
fix: Iterate, with an explicit stack only for alternatives.

title: L2: traps on numeric input: Int64(size) for 1e30 or inf in SearchForm (saved search then crashes on every load); -7 * count for huge weeks; cursor + count - 1 and abs(Int.min) in Selection.
detail: integerValue saturates to Int.max (checked). Selection traps are for extreme command parameters.
basis: read (confirmed by reading, Swift trapping semantics)

title: L3: same folder reached twice through a firmlink (/Users and /System/Volumes/Data/Users): hits reported twice with a depth limit; without a depth limit which path is reported depends on thread timing.
detail: Same device and inode (checked). De-duplication only runs for overlapping roots.

title: L4: overlapping roots drop hard links (de-dup by (device, inode) hides a second hard link at a different path).
fix: Key by path; use identity only for folders.

title: L5: end-of-search work on the main thread is O(n) several times (resultItems, rows rebuild, directory count; goToFile rebuilds item list on every Enter; Cmd+C builds one string; selectedItems walks the whole panel on every windowDidBecomeKey).
detail: Likely around a second at 5M rows.

title: L6: Spotlight path returns different results from a walk (index-handled text not re-checked: case sensitive/encoding/exact substring not enforced; root filter is a case-sensitive hasPrefix on unresolved paths; final sort not cancellable).
detail: A 'Search in' typed in another case or through a symlink finds nothing.

title: L7: regular-file check is stat-then-open; a file swapped for a FIFO in between parks a worker for good; a read on a dead NFS/SMB mount does the same (local reader opens blocking, no interrupt).
detail: Security.
fix: open(O_NONBLOCK|O_NOFOLLOW) + fstat on the descriptor, then clear O_NONBLOCK.

title: L8: [u] (precompose) never renames anything; Swift == treats NFC and NFD as equal; the test at MultiRenameEngineTests.swift:176 passes for the same reason.
fix: Compare UTF-8 bytes.

title: L9: two quick header clicks leave the list in the wrong order (second sort captured generation before first applied, so dropped; header shows descending, list ascending).

L11: preview is not cancelled when the window closes (session has no deinit; a 500k preview runs to the end); after Undo no refresh() so conflict marks stay stale.

The rename runner never replaces a different local file.
